explanation: A set answers whether the current value already has a retained occurrence. Only a duplicate must be bypassed; keeping a pointer to the last retained node makes that link change possible without searching backward.
correctness: Before each step, the retained prefix contains exactly the first occurrences in the processed original prefix, in order. The set contains precisely those values. A new value extends both the set and retained prefix. An existing value is bypassed without advancing the retained predecessor. These cases preserve the invariant and, at exhaustion, retain exactly the required original nodes.
walkthrough: For original nodes [6,2,6,3,2], retain the first 6 and the first 2. Bypass the second 6, retain 3, then bypass the final 2. The reachable original nodes have indices [0,1,3] and values [6,2,3].
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time with hash-set operations; pathological hashing can make the worst case O(n^2).
spaceComplexity: O(u) auxiliary space for u distinct values, at most O(n). No replacement list is allocated.
edgeCases: All values equal keeps only the original head.
